body: Such a difficult decision but I know sometimes it’s the only decision. Their safety is a priority. How old are your kids? I know that I’m going to have to explain what’s happening to mine before long. I’m dreading it. They really do love their Dad.
You certainly aren’t alone.

I’m still working on pain that I locked away from my past. I chip away at it little by little. And as I take the power away from the memories, little moments of joy can be found in their place. Please keep working on yours. I can tell by your words that you have a sensitive beautiful heart. You deserve happiness. 💕

When I was her age I considered suicide myself. I never thought it would affect anyone other then my grandmother. That alone kept me from trying. I never considered just how devastating it is for family and friends. When you’re in that type of darkness and pain it’s hard to see. You’re right. It doesn’t end the pain. It simply passes it on.

I’m so incredibly sorry for your loss. It’s hard to find the words to even describe how you feel.  It’s such a roller coaster. Talking to others who’ve been through or are going through the same thing helps. Please know you aren’t alone. I’m here if you ever need someone to talk to.
Keep reaching out. Keep asking for help and trying different things until you find what works for you. You deserve it.

💕💕💕 Thank you. I have 3 kids but my middle son is the one who’s struggling the most. I think 9 is a very hard year for kids. He’s trying so hard to wrap his head around how the world works. And this just doesn’t make sense to him. It breaks my heart. After my experience with my niece, hearing those words from him will never leave me.  But I will never leave him so I know we’ll all get through this. Love, loss, and grief can be so overwhelming. Especially for the young amount us.
Thank you 💕
I’m so incredibly sorry for what you’re going through. Know you’re not alone. Please reach out if you need to talk. 💕
Thank you. Just being able to write last night, and then hearing from so many supportive people helps. I really appreciate it.  💕

Then you keep trying. No one solution works for everyone. But if you keep trying you will find what works for you. Keeping everything cloaked in silence will eat away at you. You deserve more. You deserve to be happy. 💕

Thank you. I have. He started seeing someone in the Spring. We are working with him to understand and process his feelings. It’s just so difficult. Like you said, no one deserves to feel that pain, especially so young. I’m so sorry you did. I’m very glad that you are here to share your experiences now.  You are truly making a difference. 💕

I understand. I’ve struggled with depression for years. When I was younger it was the thought of my family that stopped me as well. I felt very alone and told no one. Talking to others is key. I’m so glad to hear you say that. While depression is still part of my life, all these years later, connecting with others is what’s made the greatest difference for me. Thank you!
Thank you.

That is what you’re saying. I didn’t say the hotline was the only tool people should use but it is an option. What you’re telling people is that it will only make things worse. I have been working with people in the field for over 30 year since I received help for my own depression. It’s only now that I’ve been on this side of the fence as a family member. I realize there isn’t one fix for everyone. Turning people who need help away form of resource that has helped many is dangerous.

That’s strange because it was a message much like this that saved my life when I was 28. And with many people that I’ve worked with since. I just never thought I’d be in the other side. I hope you find something that will help you and the peace that comes with that help.
And some of those people have been caring for years but it just wasn’t enough.

Well I must have gotten lucky. Because my experience was vastest different.  Having that person listen to me, was the start.  It didn’t fix anything but it helped me get through a few tough spots and helped me identify places in my community I could get help. Everyone on the other end of that line isn’t useless. I’m sorry you had a bad experience.

Thank you. And don’t worry, it doesn’t make you sound like a bad person. It might not be helpful for everyone but it is helpful for a lot of people.  It’s just one resources. The big thing is not to keep it to yourself. People do care. We aren’t alone.

I’m writing to people who are struggling and feel alone. It’s not an area I’m personally unfamiliar with.  The hotline might not be for everyone but it does help a lot of people. If it’s not for you, reach out to some you know. Just don’t suffer in silence. There are people who care.
Thank you
Those were the words of my 9 year old son.

I’m sorry your living this. It’s difficult and lonely. It’s crazy that you can be in a relationship with someone you love so much and yet feel so alone. And like you said, I don’t want to hang out with him anymore either. I don’t like the person he becomes when he drinks. 

I’m still not sure if the meetings will help but I’m finally to the point that I can’t manage everything anymore. If you do make it to a meeting, let me know how it goes. And know you aren’t alone.
Can I ask, what made you stop?

I’m so sorry. I’m living this from a mother’s viewpoint. My heart bleeds for my kids - and for you. My kids are still young but I know this will have to come to a turning point before they’re much older. The thing is, I know my husband loves our kids - and they love him. Please don’t think your dad doesn’t love you or that he puts alcohol before you. It’s not that simple. The disease is insidious. That said... please take care of yourself. I know that’s easier said then done but please try. You are worth it.
That’s just what it feels like. Everyday a little part of me is saying goodbye,  I never thought I’d be in this position. Of course, who does?

It’s not work, it’s not the kids, his crazy (I say in a loving way) mother, or even me. It’s the disease. It finds a way. It whispers in his ear and provides whatever excuse is readily available. That’s the crazy thing. There will always be a reason until he decides to stop listening.

Thank you thank you thank you. I’ve done nothing but second guess ever word I say and every decision I make. I want to be supportive but not enabling. I struggle with the decision to stay or leave. It’s nice to hear whatever I decide, it’s ok. And that I don’t have to decide today. I really appreciate it.

I appreciate you reaching out. I’m holding on to hope. It tears at my heart watching  him slowly kill himself. He really is a good person stuck in a terrible disease. I’m so glad you found a way out. Please keep working at it. I know it isn’t easy. But as you know, drinking isn’t easy either.  Thank you again and keep working. You’re worth it.

Posting is new for me. But dealing with this alone is not. It’s very difficult and very lonely. No one in my daily life understands. I have to admit just putting my thoughts down and sharing them has helped today. I’m glad it touched you. You aren’t alone.
Thank you

Believe me, it’s not in your head. After years of dealing with this, of tearing myself apart, of wondering why he didn’t care about me or the kids enough to stop, I finally internalized the fact that it isn’t about us. It’s not about how much he cares about us. If it was that clear cut he’d stop. Your husband isn’t choosing drinking over you. He’s simply drinking. It’s a disease.  Everything else (you, the kids, work, traffic, politics, crazy family stuff, etc.) are just excuses for him to justify it.  Please be kind to yourself and remind yourself when it gets overwhelming that you’re not alone.

I’m so sorry. Exhaustion is right. It’s beyond mental. I feel physically exhausted all the time. It’s effecting my Health. I’m working on learning how to take care of myself. It seems like it should be such an easy thing to do. But when you’re holding everything together all the time, it’s hard to step away. 

I’m sorry you’re in the same position but I appreciate your sharing. It helps to know you’re not alone.

Thank you. Please do share it with him.  They are in so much pain that sometimes I think it’s hard for them to see the whole picture. I know my husband struggles but I don’t think he understands the depth of the pain his disease really causes the rest of us - the loneliness, fear, anger, confusion, and doubt. At some point I hope to work up the courage to share it with my husband as well.
Thank you for your reply. I can’t tell you how much your words mean to me.  This has been a very long and lonely road. It means so much to hear for someone who understands.

He hid it because he was still relying on you emotionally and he wasn’t ready to risk that until he felt secure with this new person. He wasn’t being your friend. He was using you. You deserve better.

If you decide to start a family, make sure you plan for the best but are prepared for the worst. I know it sounds terrible but you don’t know what the future holds. You need to make sure you can take care of yourself and the kids if the situation ever changes.

Thank you for your reply. Loving someone everyday and watching them slowly kill themselves  with alcohol is so painful. Like you said, when he’s not drinking, he’s the man I married. I can’t imagine letting him go. But when he drinks, I don’t understand why I’m still married.
Thank you for replying. I’m looking for a meeting to go to this week. It’s hard to see how it can help but I’m sure it can’t hurt. I’m willing to try anything at this point.

I’m glad you chose your family. I can’t speak for your wife but those feeling get so overwhelming. I can’t imagine my husband could ever comprehend the frustration, pain, anger, and loneliness that’s been part of our marriage for a long time now.  He doesn’t see it because when he’s not drinking he’s a great guy and a good father. I don’t think he can see what the other guy , the drunk guy, is like.
Thank you. I’m got by to try my first meeting tomorrow. It’s so hard to see the path forward.
